summary: This Dockerfile creates a Python 3.11 base image that installs Docker and the Dagger CLI tool. It downloads a specific version of Dagger from GitHub, extracts it, and places it in the system path so that running the container automatically starts Dagger.

explanations.3: This pulls the official Python 3.11 image based on Debian Buster (a minimal variant) and names this stage 'base' so it can be referenced later if needed for multi-stage builds.
explanations.8: The 'set -e -x' command makes the script exit immediately if any command fails and print each command before running it, which helps catch errors and debug the build.
explanations.15: ARG creates a build-time variable that can be passed in or overridden; VERSION is set to a specific Dagger release number.
explanations.16: This constructs the filename for the Dagger archive by interpolating the VERSION variable, creating something like 'dagger_v0.15.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz'.
explanations.17: This builds the full download URL by combining the base GitHub releases URL with the archive filename, so wget knows exactly where to fetch Dagger from.
explanations.22: wget downloads the Dagger release file from the URL and saves it with the name stored in ${ARCHIVE}, using --quiet to suppress verbose output.
explanations.23: tar extracts the downloaded archive file; the 'xvfz' flags mean extract, verbose output, and automatically detect gzip compression.
explanations.27: WORKDIR sets the default working directory inside the container to /app/src, so any subsequent commands run from there.
explanations.29: ENTRYPOINT makes the container execute Dagger by default when started, rather than dropping into a shell.
